claims.text: Shockley partial dislocation loops nucleate thermally at pre-existing vacancy clusters in equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
The strain field of a vacancy cluster locally reduces stacking-fault energy and thereby lowers the critical nucleation stress.
The <11-1> orientation has a higher maximum yield stress than the <110> orientation.
The <11-1> orientation maximizes the Schmid factor on the dominant slip system and therefore requires a higher applied stress to reach the nucleation threshold than <110>.
The HCP-like regions in FeNiCrMn are intrinsic stacking faults rather than an FCC-to-HCP phase transformation.
Absence of long-range lattice-parameter shifts together with retention of FCC stacking in the surrounding matrix would identify the HCP-like regions as stacking faults.
Increasing temperature lowers the activation barrier or critical resolved shear stress for dislocation nucleation.
Stacking-fault energy in a similar CoCrFeMnNi system is approximately -15 to 2 mJ/m^2 from 77 to 293 K.
Low stacking-fault energy stabilizes an intrinsic stacking fault as a metastable defect rather than a phase boundary.
The <11-1> yield stress will exceed the <110> yield stress by approximately 10–15%.
Dislocation-nucleation events will be spatially correlated with vacancy clusters.
The HCP-like regions will exhibit local changes from ABC to AB stacking.
The HCP-like regions will produce no global lattice-parameter shift characteristic of a phase transformation.
Flow or peak stress decreases as temperature increases from 77 K to 300 K.
FeNiCrMn will not exhibit the flow-stress serrations associated with twinning or phase transformation.
CoNiCrFeMn nanowires exhibit serrated flow together with deformation twinning and FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Yield strength is insensitive to strain rate over 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1.
Deformation is mediated by partial dislocations and intrinsic stacking faults.
Vacancy clusters are the dominant nucleation sites in single-crystal nanowires or similarly small volumes.
Above 1000 K, vacancy-cluster effects are suppressed and homogeneous nucleation or phase transformation is promoted.

contradictions.description: The orientation argument says that maximizing the Schmid factor makes <11-1> require a higher applied stress to reach the nucleation threshold. Within the stated resolved-shear-stress framework, a larger Schmid factor would ordinarily imply that the same threshold resolved shear stress is reached at a lower applied stress, so the stated mechanism does not coherently produce the predicted higher yield stress.
